preference_statement: Nuclear energy is explicitly favored as a clean-firm decarbonization and energy-security option where assurance gates can be met.
guardrail_summary: safety waste water security cost schedule open contracting workforce emergency planning host-community and civil-rights gates cap maturity

preference_statement: Existing nuclear fleet continuity, safe life extension and uprates rank ahead of speculative new generation when they preserve low-carbon firm capacity at lower delivery risk.
guardrail_summary: regulator-visible safety case, maintenance, workforce and market viability required

preference_statement: Advanced reactors and SMRs are favored as option value only when public evidence covers licensing, financing, siting, fuel, engagement and supply chain readiness.
guardrail_summary: SMR readiness evidence must not be inferred from vendor claims alone

preference_statement: Nuclear is favored through an explicit deployment sequence: existing fleet preservation, uprates, safe restarts, repeatable new build, then SMR/advanced deployments where readiness evidence is real.
burden_of_proof_shift: explain why earlier nuclear sequence options are unavailable before relying on fossil fallback or unproven advanced projects
guardrail_summary: fuel cycle, water/site, grid/load, anti-crowding-out and exception-ledger gates cap maturity

preference_statement: Nuclear remains favored, but regulatory licensing, public participation, security, waste-consent, emergency preparedness and red-team traceability are hard maturity caps, not optional communications tasks.
burden_of_proof_shift: explain how nuclear project claims satisfy license basis, public docket, security, waste, emergency and counterargument gates before lifting maturity
guardrail_summary: Part 53/license basis, public participation, consent-based waste siting, physical protection, material accountability, emergency preparedness and red-team gates cap maturity

preference_statement: Nuclear deployment is explicitly favored when clean-firm demand can be paired with bankable capital stack, creditworthy offtake, standardized construction and public-value protections.
burden_of_proof_shift: explain why clean-firm procurement excludes bankable nuclear or why nuclear cannot meet gates
guardrail_summary: bankability, offtake, construction, public value, ratepayer, supply chain and project-control gates cap maturity

preference_statement: Large loads and data centers should be routed to nuclear clean-firm assessment by default when they need high-capacity-factor low-carbon supply.
burden_of_proof_shift: large-load plans must explain why nuclear, uprates, restarts, repeat builds or SMRs are not part of the clean-firm option set
guardrail_summary: grid deliverability, public value, ratepayer protection, flexibility and local evidence remain mandatory

preference_statement: Nuclear is favored only with explicit fuel-cycle and backend realism: uranium, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, fabrication, safeguards, spent-fuel, transport, consent and funding evidence must be traceable.
burden_of_proof_shift: show credible fuel supply, fuel qualification, backend, safeguards, transport, consent and publication-control evidence before maturity upgrades
guardrail_summary: fuel-cycle and backend gaps cap nuclear maturity even where policy preference is favorable

preference_statement: Nuclear is favored as an energy-security and anti-coercion resource when allied fuel-cycle, vendor-continuity, export-finance, safeguards and sensitive-publication gates are closed.
burden_of_proof_shift: projects opposing nuclear in clean-firm energy-security contexts must address why equivalent reliability and anti-coercion benefits can be achieved without nuclear; nuclear projects must still close all geopolitical gates
guardrail_summary: fuel, sanctions, vendor lock-in, 123-agreement, export finance, safeguards, nonproliferation, publication and red-team gaps cap nuclear maturity

preference_statement: Nuclear is favored only when the human system can build, license, inspect, operate, maintain, learn and govern it.
applies_to: all nuclear service floors; existing fleet; new build; SMR; industrial heat; data centers; fuel cycle; backend
burden_of_proof_shift: show workforce and institutional capacity before claiming mature nuclear readiness
guardrail_summary: operator licensing, regulator capacity, craft labor, QA/safety culture, knowledge retention, emergency planning and publication-control gates cap maturity

preference_statement: Nuclear remains explicitly favored only where cyber, digital I&C, OT, software supply-chain, AI/autonomy, vendor-access, grid/telecom, incident recovery and security-safe publication gates can be met.
burden_of_proof_shift: prove cyber/digital assurance before crediting nuclear maturity, digital modernization or AI-era reliability benefit
guardrail_summary: critical digital asset inventory, OT/IT boundary, SBOM/provenance, vulnerability governance, remote access, incident recovery, AI boundary, and sensitive publication controls cap maturity

preference_statement: Nuclear remains explicitly favored only where physical protection, design-basis-threat alignment, insider mitigation, drone/perimeter posture, transport security, law-enforcement interface, and security-safe publication gates can be met.
burden_of_proof_shift: prove physical-security assurance before crediting nuclear maturity or public-value claims
guardrail_summary: physical protection, force-on-force/equivalent testing, access authorization, insider mitigation, transport security, law-enforcement coordination and redacted public scorecards cap maturity
